subject: zoology
question_text: Why is the syngamy found in Plasmodium called anisogamy?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Syngamy
lines: Syngamy is the complete fusion of a male gamete
with a female gamete to form a zygote.
In Plasmodium this fusion takes place in the
crop of the female Anopheles mosquito.
steps.why: The answer starts from the general word so the special word has something to be measured against, and it fixes the place where the fusion happens.
common_mistakes: Writing that syngamy takes place in man. It takes place in the mosquito.
Confusing syngamy with schizogony. Syngamy is fusion; schizogony is splitting.
steps.memory_tip: Syn- means together: syngamy is two gametes fusing into one zygote.
steps.margin_note: One line for the definition, one for the place. Two lines.

steps.label: Why anisogamy

lines.text: Unequal gametes fuse, so it is anisogamy

lines: The male gamete of Plasmodium is small and the
female gamete is large, so the two are
Fusion of two gametes that are unlike in size is
steps.why: Aniso- means unequal, so the reason is a comparison of the two gametes: name both sizes and the term follows on its own.
common_mistakes: Writing that the gametes are alike. Alike gametes would make it isogamy.
Giving the reason as a difference in number instead of a difference in size.
steps.memory_tip: Iso- equal, aniso- unequal: small male, large female, so anisogamy.
steps.margin_note: Name both sizes, then close with the term. Two lines.

insider_note: The mark is on the word 'dissimilar in size'; a correct definition of syngamy with no size comparison does not answer the question asked.
